_about: The fans the crowd's parts are cut from (tools/prep_crowd.py makes assets/stadium/crowd_kit.glb from this). Every fan is one whole Tripo character; its head, torso (the outfit) and legs become parts that fit any other part of the same gender. `template` is the prompt, with `{who}` from the fan. `source` is the raw model, from the project root; a fan without one is skipped. `use` lists the parts of the fan that go into the kit. `yaw` turns the model to face -Y in Blender. `joints` overrides a joint prep_crowd.py found (names as printed after JOINTS; [x, y, z] with the height = 1, front = -Y, the fan's left = +X). `keys` overrides a colour it sampled (`skin`, `hair`, `shirt`, `pants`: [r, g, b] 0..1 as in the texture; `hair`: null for a bald head). `options` tunes how its texture is read: `chroma` (0.07: how far from a sampled colour a pixel may be and still count as it; lower when skin gets painted as shirt) and `luma` ([0.4, 1.8]: how much darker and brighter). `beard` (true for a fan whose beard hangs below the chin, so that it goes with the head and not with the shirt; only if the hair is not the colour of the shirt). `budgets` gives a fan triangle budgets of its own (same shape as the `budgets` below; what it leaves out is as for everybody). A `placeholder` fan is used only while its gender has no other fan with a source.
template: a sports fan, {who}, standing upright in a T-pose with arms straight out to the sides and legs slightly apart, clean shaven, smooth skin, chunky stylized cartoon character, simple shapes, single isolated figure

m0.who: (the dudeman player model, standing in until the real fans are generated)
